content: Trinity Mother Frances Health System is a non-profit regional healthcare provider based in Tyler, Texas. It operates two hospitals and 22 regional health clinics across north-central and northeast Texas. In the early 1930s, the Sisters of the Holy Family of Nazareth identified the need for a hospital in Tyler, Texas. The hospital was constructed through a collaborative effort involving the Sisters, the City of Tyler, and local medical professionals. It was named in honor of Frances Siedliska, the founder of the Sisters of the Holy Family of Nazareth. Mother Frances Hospital officially opened on March 18, 1937, a day earlier than planned, due to an explosion in nearby New London. In 1948, the Sisters of the Holy Family of Nazareth completed the purchase of the hospital from the City of Tyler. In October 1965, the hospital celebrated Mother Frances Week in Tyler, marking the dedication of a new 140,000-square-foot wing. This $5 million expansion added 110 new patient beds and a cafeteria to the facility. In 1934, Dr. William Howard Bryant and Dr. Sidney W. Bradford established the Bryant Clinic. This clinic, along with the newly opened Mother Frances Hospital, was among the first responders to the New London School Explosion. In 1948, the clinic was renamed the Medical and Surgical Clinic. Later, with the integration of two other Tyler-area medical practices, it became known as Trinity Clinic. In 1995, Mother Frances Hospital and Trinity Clinic merged to form Trinity Mother Frances Health System, one of the first integrated healthcare systems in the United States. The flagship hospital of the system, Mother Frances Hospital Tyler, is a 392-bed acute care facility located on Hospital Row in Tyler, Texas. It features a Level II Trauma Center and an accredited Chest Pain Center.
